subject: Management response: SOC 2 control deviation and evidence handoff
messages:
From: Amanda Lee <amanda@greenfin.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: GreenFin Security Team <security@greenfin.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 exception discovered — request for management response and evidence

Hi Hannah,

During our control review for the upcoming vendor risk assessment we noticed an exception flagged in control CC6 (backup verification) for the period May 12–May 28, 2026. Our auditor is asking for a formal management response, details of remediation (if any), and evidence that demonstrates corrective action. Specifically we need:

- A one-page management response describing the cause and corrective actions taken.
- Dates/timestamps showing when the remediation was applied.
- Any change logs, incident postmortem, or ticket IDs tied to the remediation.
- A bridge letter if the remediation completed after the SOC 2 audit period, clarifying whether the exception impacts the report conclusions.

Can your team provide the management response and the evidence by EOD Monday 2026-06-15? If remediation is still in progress, please provide the status and expected completion date. We may need to include your response in our attestation deliverable, so clear wording around timelines is important.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to take a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Amanda Lee
Director, Vendor Risk Management
GreenFin Capital
[Attachment: audit_finding_summary.pdf (PDF, 98 KB)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda@greenfin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 exception discovered — request for management response and evidence

Amanda —

Thanks for the flag and the clear ask. We take exceptions like this seriously. Below is an initial management response and the evidence we can provide today; Monica is looping in remediation details and Rishi is on the audit/bridge-letter thread for legal/attestation language.

Management response (summary):
- Issue: A repeated failure in our automated backup verification job caused missed integrity checks for backups created between 2026-05-12 and 2026-05-28. Root cause was a transient regression introduced in the verification agent during a scheduled update.
- Impact: Backup verification checks for the window noted were incomplete; no customer data loss was detected and all backups remained accessible.
- Corrective actions taken: Rolled back the verification agent on 2026-05-29, re-ran verification jobs for affected snapshots, and implemented an additional CI gate for the verification agent to prevent the regression from being deployed.
- Status: Verification re-checks completed on 2026-05-31 and all snapshots validated.

Evidence attached/provided:
- remediation_plan_v1.pdf — remediation summary and action items (attached).
- control_logs_202605.zip — logs and verification run output for May 12–31 (attached).
- Ticket: INF-4521 — root cause and rollback notes (link in Drive).

Requested timeline:
- Remediation completed (verification re-runs) on 2026-05-31. We can provide timestamped logs showing re-check completion.
- If GreenFin requires a formal bridge letter, we propose the draft language below and can route through Legal for signature.

Proposed short draft bridge letter (for your review):
"During the SOC 2 audit period ending May 31, 2026, Redwood Inference identified an operational deviation affecting an automated backup verification process. The deviation was detected on May 28, 2026 and corrected by rolling back a verification agent on May 29, 2026. All affected backups were re-verified and validation completed on May 31, 2026. Based on remediation and verification activities, Redwood Inference asserts that the deviation was remediated prior to the end of the audit period and did not result in loss of customer data or affect the operating effectiveness conclusions."

Next steps:
1) Monica to attach the incident postmortem and confirm evidence file contents.
2) Rishi to review and propose final attestation/bridge-letter wording if Legal needs more specific phrasing.
3) Hannah to schedule a 20-min call if GreenFin wants a walkthrough.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0119
[Attachment: remediation_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 124 KB)]

Amanda / Hannah —

Adding the technical remediation details and confirming the evidence package contents.

What we ran and attached:
- control_logs_202605.zip: includes verification run stdout, checksums, and timestamped success records for the re-run completed 2026-05-31T22:14:03Z.
- Postmortem: INF-4521-postmortem.pdf (internal) — root cause analysis and preventative actions.
- Change history: git commit IDs and deployment record showing the rollback on 2026-05-29 02:41:10Z.

Audit period clarification: our SOC 2 Type II audit period is Apr 1, 2025 — May 31, 2026. The remediation completed on May 31, 2026 before the audit period closed; therefore, our position is that the exception was remediated within the audit period. We will still provide a short bridge letter if you prefer explicit language for your auditor.

Proposed language tweak (if you need explicit date-first wording):
"Remediation activities were completed and validated on 2026-05-31 prior to the close of the SOC 2 Type II audit period (ending 2026-05-31). No customer data loss was detected and successful verification records are included in the attached logs."

Attachments uploaded to shared Drive: remediation_plan_v1.pdf, control_logs_202605.zip, INF-4521-postmortem.pdf. Link above.

If GreenFin wants Legal to sign a bridge letter, please confirm and we'll circulate the draft to our Legal (cc Rishi) for signature.

—Monica

2) We'll need a signed bridge letter (our auditor prefers Legal-signed letters). Can Rishi or someone from Legal sign the proposed draft and return a signed PDF?
